newsitem.title: CANADA: CRU forecasts magnesium at $1.60/lb in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: CRU forecasts magnesium at $1.60/lb in 1997/98.

text.p: TORONTO, Despite a turnaround in the magnesium market over the past few months, the price of magnesium will not spiral upwards but edge higher to $1.60 per pound for spot Western primary grade in the United States during this year and next, analyst Mark Croft of CRU International said.

"We expect the market to recover, but we don't see in the short-term another (record) year like 1994," Croft said. The magnesium market grew by 10 to 15 percent in 1994, compared to a 2 percent dip in 1996, Croft said.
After 1998, prices will gradually rise by 10 to 20 cents per poound by the year 2000, Croft told delegates at the World Magnesium Conference here.
Primary magnesium prices in the U.S. are currently about $1.55 per pound, down from $1.70 at the end of last year, and $2.20 in January 1996.

Croft estimated that production costs, including capital, for a greenfield magnesium plant are about $1.50 per pound. Many existing integrated producers have operating costs of below $1.00 per pound, he added.
But the industry is still operating at a relatively low capacity utilization rate of 80 percent this year, rising to 85 percent in 2000, Croft said.
